text:
elaine: quick heads-up 1: bringing up ashwood-7b in staging (7B dense). Ran a 4-bit PTQ run and saw usable perf but a consistent regression on our abstractive summarization suite (~3.8 BLEU-equivalent drop). Also noticed a LICENSE clause that might block redistributing quantized/converted weights: 'You may not redistribute derived weights or transformed model files without explicit permission from the copyright holder.' can legal take a look? link to license & card uploaded to the ticket
noah: can you paste the exact license text here and attach the eval diffs? I can try narrower prompt repros and check if the regressions are prompt-sensitive
elaine: pasted snippet above. eval diffs uploaded to ML-8721: shows regressions concentrated on instruction-style long-form summarization (T0-ish prompts). small-chat and classification unaffected.
mike: infra Q: if redistribution of derived weights is prohibited, does that mean we can still host quantized checkpoints for Dedicated customers (we'd keep artifacts in our storage) but not hand them over? or is hosting considered redistribution? @sara-legal
sara-legal: short answer: ambiguous. "Redistribute" usually means providing copies to third parties. Hosting behind an API is generally allowed unless the license explicitly prohibits offering service. But the phrasing around "transformed model files" looks like they intended to stop distribution of quantized or otherwise transformed weights. We should avoid packaging quantized artifacts for download or including them in customer deliverables for now
sara-legal: action items from my side: 1) review full LICENSE and model card (please confirm link source), 2) confirm provenance of weights (upstream release vs third-party upload), 3) draft a permission request template for redistrib of transformed weights if needed
elaine: weights are from a community HF repo with no CLA. model_card indicates original authors uploaded with standard header, but not an explicit redistrib grant. I also captured host vs deliverable testcases where we attempted to bundle a quantized .pt for offline eval.
noah: operationally, for Dedicated we can keep quantized artifacts in S3 and enable inference from those images; for Private/on-prem customers we might need a different approach (managed-delivery or building quantization inside the customer's infra without handing out artifacts). If legal says we can't distribute, we'll implement "managed-quantize" flow (run quantization in-customer or via ephemeral import)
mike: tagging rollout: I'll block the packaging pipeline that produces downloadable qpt bundles until we have legal confirmation. For hosted API and Dedicated hosting it's fine to use quantized runtime internally, but won't expose downloads
sara-legal: agreed. Meanwhile I recommend we run a narrow regression triage: compare FP16 vs 4-bit outputs for the failing prompts to check whether the issue is quant noise or compiler kernel mismatch. If it's quant noise, we can attempt per-layer quant calibration or fallback for summarization workloads
elaine: already running ablations (per-layer, GPTQ-like vs PTQ calibration). will post diffs to ML-8721. pausing any packaging tests now.
deploy-bot: Ticket ML-8721 created for follow-up: https://redwood.internal/ml/tickets/8721
sara-legal: I'll draft the outreach email to upstream authors requesting permission to redistribute derived weights for enterprise customers, include a template addendum for an enterprise redistrib license. Will cc eng-ml when draft is ready
noah: :thumbsup: will help with technical repro and add a small eval harness to the ticket to capture model RNG seeds and deterministic settings
mike: :eyes: thanks folks, will update deployment plan once legal confirms
elaine: thanks1: will keep the ticket updated with regression artifacts and quant configs
sara-legal: thanks all. keep infra blocked on packaging until we have explicit permission or a legal-safe workflow documented
noah: cheers
